s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive lower limb mass with ulceration and systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Firm mass over the distal tibia with ulceration and discharge
Reduced knee range of motion and tenderness over the left knee and proximal tibia
Large metadiaphyseal lesion of the tibia with soft-tissue opacity and bone erosion on radiographs
key_facts: 51-year-old man with 1-year history of progressive pain and swelling below the left knee
Firm mass measuring 30 × 18 × 12 cm over the distal tibia
Anterior discharging ulcer 12 cm in diameter with areas of necrosis
Tenderness over the left knee and proximal tibia
Laboratory studies, including complete blood count and metabolic panel, within normal limits
Plain radiographs showed large metadiaphyseal lesion of the tibia with soft-tissue opacity and bone erosion

shortlist.label: Osteosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large metadiaphyseal lesion of the tibia with soft-tissue opacity and bone erosion, consistent with aggressive bone tumor

shortlist.label: Chondrosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and radiographic appearance of a large mass with ulceration and areas of necrosis, suggestive of cartilaginous tumor

shortlist.label: Ewing's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive bone lesion with soft-tissue involvement and systemic symptoms, such as intermittent fevers

shortlist.label: Parosteal osteosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Location of the tumor on the surface of the bone, with extension into the proximal leg soft tissues, consistent with parosteal osteosarcoma

shortlist.label: Chordoma
shortlist.why_kept: Slow-growing tumor with areas of necrosis and ulceration, although less likely given the aggressive nature of the presentation

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a large, firm mass and a discharging ulcer, along with radiographic findings of bone erosion and destruction, is more typical of osteosarcoma, which is known for its aggressive behavior and potential for soft tissue extension.

rejected.label: Chondrosarcoma
rejected.why: Chondrosarcoma tends to be slower-growing and less aggressive than osteosarcoma, which does not align with the patient's rapid progression and ulceration.

rejected.label: Ewing's sarcoma
rejected.why: Ewing's sarcoma typically affects younger patients and often presents with systemic symptoms such as fever and weight loss, which are not prominent in this case.

rejected.label: Parosteal osteosarcoma
rejected.why: Parosteal osteosarcoma usually has a more indolent course and often presents as a bony mass without significant soft tissue involvement, which contrasts with this patient's extensive soft tissue disease.

rejected.label: Chordoma
rejected.why: Chordoma is a rare tumor that typically affects the axial skeleton, particularly the spine and base of the skull, and is less likely to present with the aggressive features seen in this patient's leg.
